title: A new career path is tempting young bankers away from Wall Street
excerpt: AI startups like Rogo are attracting young bankers from some of Wall Street's biggest firms, and providing an option beyond buy- or sell-side.
content_html:
By Alice Tecotzky

2026-08-10T09:03:01.233Z

Read in app

Young bankers are facing a new choice.

Wall Street has traditionally offered a clear, if grueling, career path for junior employees: get an internship, work in investment banking for two years, and decide whether to stay in banking, move to the buy side, or get an MBA. AI is now disrupting not only the day-to-day nature of the work, but also potentially opening a new fork in the finance career road, as some young financiers flock to AI startups for financial firms.

Jared Swansen, 27, made the jump to Rogo, one of those startups, in January. He's since forgotten all the Excel shortcuts he used as a banker and investor, now that the hours he spent typing away are instead spent on the phone with people he used to sit across from, teaching them how to cut the drudgery out of dealmaking.

"The holy grail was to go to the buy side. That was everyone's dream," Swansen, who spent around three years at Bank of America before moving to a small buy-side firm, said. "It was exactly what I had hoped, doing all the analysis and working on the different transactions that I hoped to when I was starting out my banking career. But it was hard to not see what was happening with AI."

Rogo was founded in 2021 by former investment bankers in their twenties from Lazard and JPMorgan and has secured a $2 billion valuation after its Series D fundraising round in April. It touts domain expertise as a big draw, since the workforce is predominantly split between engineers and former financiers like Swansen. According to employees' LinkedIn profiles, they hail from Evercore, Goldman Sachs, and Citi, among other firms.

Rogo's leadership doesn't expect or want all bankers or private-market investors to suddenly jump ship to join a startup — that reality would erode their client base. Recruiters who work in finance aren't seeing a mass exodus among younger employees, though they said that AI is becoming an increasingly attractive option for the more entrepreneurially minded. Yet leaving the well-charted, lucrative finance road comes with its risks.

"It comes down to how common and how broad-based this is. It's hard to quantify," Anthony Keizner, co-founder of recruiting firm Odyssey Search Partners, said.

Rogo has more than 300 clients, including Lazard, Moelis, and Tiger Global, and automates much of the tedious work, like making slide decks, producing research, and building models. Users can email instructions to its AI agent, Felix, the same way they do colleagues.

There are other players in the vertical AI-for-finance space. Competitors like Hebbia and Farsight AI also promise to speed up work, and large AI labs, including Anthropic and OpenAI, are hiring bankers to work on services for financial firms.

Rogo is something of a tech-finance mashup — former bankers walk around in jeans and enjoy daily free lunch, while engineers grind out finance hours in conference rooms named "Dimon" and "Soros." When asked whether they work at a finance or tech company, the four employees interviewed for this piece paused, before Elsa McLean, the head of talent, eventually settled on "an AI company."

McLean, 30, said she's stopped having to educate potential recruits about what the Rogo does, and has seen a "massive uptick in inbound applications" starting in the first half of this year. The company has doubled its headcount in the past year to more than 150, and plans to double it again within the next 12 months. It has offices in New York and London, with plans to open locations in San Francisco and Singapore.

Hebbia was founded in 2020 and has clients in investing, banking, and the broader deal ecosystem, including law. It's also seen rapid growth: the startup has around 200 employees, compared to just shy of 100 a year ago. Tom Navin, the head of people, said that monthly inbound applications have nearly tripled this year to an average of 7,000, and around 60% of employees have a background in finance.

Swansen "caught the bug" for the finance industry during his senior year of high school, and expected to chart a traditional career. He first discovered Rogo while working as an investor at Acacia Research, and though leaving wasn't easy, the idea of being at the center of technological transformation was more exciting.

Rachel Friedman, 27, wasn't letting go of her preconceived future when she came to Rogo as one of eight employees and the first woman. She spent more than two years at Jefferies as an investment banker and knew she didn't want to stay in finance, though she's glad she started there.

For her, Rogo was more about joining an interesting, fast-paced place where she could play any part, with the added perk of swapping her trousers for the occasional sweatpant. Starting at Rogo now, with its big-name investors and global offices, isn't quite the same gamble.

"My impression is that the risk profile of candidates has pretty significantly changed over time," Friedman said. "Now, everyone is comfortable with the idea that every financial institution will adopt AI. The risk is around betting on the right one. We feel really good about that, obviously."

Swansen said that by the time he joined Rogo, "it felt like probably the bigger risk was doing nothing when the whole world was changing."

In some ways, working at Rogo isn't all that different from working at a top financial firm, and Friedman said most people don't see it as a departure from finance. The cumulative hours are similar, though employees generally have more control over when they work.

"I work a lot, but I'm never scared at 6 p.m. on a Friday that something is going to blow up and destroy my weekend," Swansen said. "I think I could probably end work every day three hours earlier if I wanted to. But because we're growing really fast, there are just cool opportunities everywhere." (Friedman, Swansen's boss, is worried he works too much, since he's usually up until around 1:00 a.m.)

Those who come from the world of high finance leverage their old connections when covering and securing clients, including Jack Maroni, 27, an MBA intern who spent four years at KKR before attending Harvard Business School. He said he's introduced Rogo to friends who are still on the buy side. Swansen has found that his background in banking and private equity is key to keeping clients happy with Rogo, since he understands the details of their workflows.

The work ethic is also similar, employees said, since many came from a world of 80-hour workweeks and, to quote Maroni, "built the muscle around grinding."

The paycheck, however, isn't necessarily as familiar.

At Rogo, a "forward-deployed banker" in New York would earn a base salary between $115,000 and $180,000, plus potential equity and bonus, according to a job posting. Candidates are expected to have at least three years of investment banking experience at a top firm. Rogo declined to provide further details on its pay packages.

Second-year associates at top firms can make up to $400,000 all-in, Meridith Dennes, managing partner at Prospect Rock Partners, said. This year is proving especially profitable, as banks report record profits. None of the recruiters said they've seen hordes of young people leave their jobs because of anxiety about AI — banking is, Dennes said, "always going to be a stable choice."

"It is challenging to try and pull the top investment banker who's being paid an incredibly high bonus, being well taken care of. It's going to be really difficult to pull that person out unless they have a real passion for AI," said Brianne Sterling, who leads the investment banking practice at recruiting firm Selby Jennings.

One key question, Keizner said, is how much equity employees get and its potential value, since cash compensation alone probably isn't enough to lure people to startups like Rogo. An equity grant in a company that succeeds could be "as lucrative, if not more lucrative, than being on a traditional finance path," he said.

Navin, the head of people at Hebbia, said the compensation packages can require "a very different framing mentally" for former bankers or investors, who are more used to cash than equity. Hebbia offers bonuses for forward-deployed banking and investing roles, but they're "a lot smaller" than in traditional finance, partly because of the inclusion of equity.

More than anything, Friedman said, people struggle to give up the structure of finance. They're used to knowing what it means to do well, what the promotion path looks like, exactly how their pay will change over the years.

"Convincing them that it'll be okay in a place where there's far less structure and your path might look different than your neighbor's — having that conversation with folks, some people definitely have to get over that mental barrier that unstructured things can be good," she said.

sentences.en: When asked whether they work at a finance or tech company, the four employees interviewed for this piece paused, before Elsa McLean, the head of talent, eventually settled on "an AI company."
sentences.zh: 当被问及他们是在金融公司还是科技公司工作时，接受本文采访的四名员工停了下来，人才主管艾尔莎·麦克莱恩 (Elsa McLean) 最终选择了“一家人工智能公司”。

sentences.en: In addition to the ping pong table, Rogo's office in Manhattan has board games and an Xbox.
sentences.zh: 除了乒乓球桌外，Rogo 在曼哈顿的办公室还配有棋盘游戏和 Xbox。

sentences.en: Corrie Aune for BI
sentences.zh: BI 的 Corrie Aune

blocks.html_en: McLean, 30, said she's stopped having to educate potential recruits about what the Rogo does, and has seen a "massive uptick in inbound applications" starting in the first half of this year. The company has doubled its headcount in the past year to more than 150, and plans to double it again within the next 12 months. It has offices in New York and London, with plans to open locations in San Francisco and Singapore.

sentences.en: McLean, 30, said she's stopped having to educate potential recruits about what the Rogo does, and has seen a "massive uptick in inbound applications" starting in the first half of this year.
sentences.zh: 30 岁的麦克莱恩表示，她不再需要对潜在的新员工进行有关 Rogo 用途的教育，并且从今年上半年开始，“入境申请数量大幅增加”。

sentences.en: The company has doubled its headcount in the past year to more than 150, and plans to double it again within the next 12 months.
sentences.zh: 该公司去年员工人数增加了一倍，达到 150 多人，并计划在未来 12 个月内再次增加一倍。

sentences.en: It has offices in New York and London, with plans to open locations in San Francisco and Singapore.
sentences.zh: 该公司在纽约和伦敦设有办事处，并计划在旧金山和新加坡开设办事处。

blocks.html_en: Hebbia was founded in 2020 and has clients in investing, banking, and the broader deal ecosystem, including law. It's also seen rapid growth: the startup has around 200 employees, compared to just shy of 100 a year ago. Tom Navin, the head of people, said that monthly inbound applications have nearly tripled this year to an average of 7,000, and around 60% of employees have a background in finance.

sentences.en: Hebbia was founded in 2020 and has clients in investing, banking, and the broader deal ecosystem, including law.
sentences.zh: Hebbia 成立于 2020 年，拥有投资、银行和更广泛的交易生态系统（包括法律）的客户。

sentences.en: It's also seen rapid growth: the startup has around 200 employees, compared to just shy of 100 a year ago.
sentences.zh: 它还实现了快速增长：该初创公司拥有约 200 名员工，而一年前只有不到 100 名员工。

sentences.en: Tom Navin, the head of people, said that monthly inbound applications have nearly tripled this year to an average of 7,000, and around 60% of employees have a background in finance.
sentences.zh: 人事主管 Tom Navin 表示，今年每月入境申请数量几乎增加了两倍，达到平均 7,000 份，大约 60% 的员工拥有金融背景。

blocks.html_en: Swansen "caught the bug" for the finance industry during his senior year of high school, and expected to chart a traditional career. He first discovered Rogo while working as an investor at Acacia Research, and though leaving wasn't easy, the idea of being at the center of technological transformation was more exciting.

sentences.en: Swansen "caught the bug" for the finance industry during his senior year of high school, and expected to chart a traditional career.
sentences.zh: 斯旺森在高中四年级时“迷上了”金融行业，并希望开创传统的职业生涯。

sentences.en: He first discovered Rogo while working as an investor at Acacia Research, and though leaving wasn't easy, the idea of being at the center of technological transformation was more exciting.
sentences.zh: 他第一次发现 Rogo 是在 Acacia Research 担任投资者时，虽然离开并不容易，但成为技术转型中心的想法更令人兴奋。

blocks.html_en: Rachel Friedman, 27, wasn't letting go of her preconceived future when she came to Rogo as one of eight employees and the first woman. She spent more than two years at Jefferies as an investment banker and knew she didn't want to stay in finance, though she's glad she started there.

sentences.en: Rachel Friedman, 27, wasn't letting go of her preconceived future when she came to Rogo as one of eight employees and the first woman.
sentences.zh: 27 岁的雷切尔·弗里德曼 (Rachel Friedman) 作为八名员工之一、也是第一位女性来到 Rogo 时，并没有放弃她先入为主的未来。

sentences.en: She spent more than two years at Jefferies as an investment banker and knew she didn't want to stay in finance, though she's glad she started there.
sentences.zh: 她在杰富瑞 (Jefferies) 担任了两年多的投资银行家，她知道自己不想留在金融业，尽管她很高兴自己从那里开始。

sentences.en: Rachel Friedman joined Rogo when there were only eight employees.
sentences.zh: 当 Rogo 只有 8 名员工时，Rachel Friedman 就加入了。

sentences.en: Corrie Aune for BI
sentences.zh: BI 的 Corrie Aune

blocks.html_en: For her, Rogo was more about joining an interesting, fast-paced place where she could play any part, with the added perk of swapping her trousers for the occasional sweatpant. Starting at Rogo now, with its big-name investors and global offices, isn't quite the same gamble.

sentences.en: For her, Rogo was more about joining an interesting, fast-paced place where she could play any part, with the added perk of swapping her trousers for the occasional sweatpant.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，罗戈更多的是加入一个有趣的、快节奏的地方，在那里她可以扮演任何角色，还有一个额外的好处，就是偶尔把裤子换成运动裤。

sentences.en: Starting at Rogo now, with its big-name investors and global offices, isn't quite the same gamble.
sentences.zh: 现在从 Rogo 开始，拥有大牌投资者和全球办事处，这并不完全是一场赌博。

blocks.html_en: "My impression is that the risk profile of candidates has pretty significantly changed over time," Friedman said. "Now, everyone is comfortable with the idea that every financial institution will adopt AI. The risk is around betting on the right one. We feel really good about that, obviously."

sentences.en: "My impression is that the risk profile of candidates has pretty significantly changed over time," Friedman said.
sentences.zh: “我的印象是，候选人的风险状况随着时间的推移发生了相当大的变化，”弗里德曼说。

sentences.en: "Now, everyone is comfortable with the idea that every financial institution will adopt AI.
sentences.zh: “现在，每个人都对每个金融机构都将采用人工智能的想法感到满意。

sentences.en: The risk is around betting on the right one.
sentences.zh: 风险在于押注于正确的人。

sentences.en: We feel really good about that, obviously."
sentences.zh: 显然，我们对此感觉非常好。”

blocks.html_en: Swansen said that by the time he joined Rogo, "it felt like probably the bigger risk was doing nothing when the whole world was changing."

sentences.en: Swansen said that by the time he joined Rogo, "it felt like probably the bigger risk was doing nothing when the whole world was changing."
sentences.zh: 斯旺森说，当他加入罗戈时，“感觉更大的风险可能是当整个世界都在变化时什么也不做。”

blocks.html_en: In some ways, working at Rogo isn't all that different from working at a top financial firm, and Friedman said most people don't see it as a departure from finance. The cumulative hours are similar, though employees generally have more control over when they work.

sentences.en: In some ways, working at Rogo isn't all that different from working at a top financial firm, and Friedman said most people don't see it as a departure from finance.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，在 Rogo 工作与在顶级金融公司工作并没有什么不同，弗里德曼表示，大多数人并不认为这与金融业有任何区别。

sentences.en: The cumulative hours are similar, though employees generally have more control over when they work.
sentences.zh: 累计工作时间相似，但员工通常对工作时间有更多的控制权。

blocks.html_en: "I work a lot, but I'm never scared at 6 p.m. on a Friday that something is going to blow up and destroy my weekend," Swansen said. "I think I could probably end work every day three hours earlier if I wanted to. But because we're growing really fast, there are just cool opportunities everywhere." (Friedman, Swansen's boss, is worried he works too much, since he's usually up until around 1:00 a.m.)

sentences.en: "I work a lot, but I'm never scared at 6 p.m.
sentences.zh: “我工作很多，但下午 6 点我从不害怕。

sentences.en: on a Friday that something is going to blow up and destroy my weekend," Swansen said.
sentences.zh: 周五，有什么事情会爆炸并毁掉我的周末，”斯旺森说。

sentences.en: "I think I could probably end work every day three hours earlier if I wanted to.
sentences.zh: “我想如果我愿意的话，我可以每天提前三个小时结束工作。

sentences.en: But because we're growing really fast, there are just cool opportunities everywhere."
sentences.zh: 但因为我们发展得非常快，所以到处都有很棒的机会。”

sentences.en: (Friedman, Swansen's boss, is worried he works too much, since he's usually up until around 1:00 a.m.)
sentences.zh: （斯旺森的老板弗里德曼担心他工作太多，因为他通常要工作到凌晨 1:00 左右。）

blocks.html_en: Those who come from the world of high finance leverage their old connections when covering and securing clients, including Jack Maroni, 27, an MBA intern who spent four years at KKR before attending Harvard Business School. He said he's introduced Rogo to friends who are still on the buy side. Swansen has found that his background in banking and private equity is key to keeping clients happy with Rogo, since he understands the details of their workflows.

sentences.en: Those who come from the world of high finance leverage their old connections when covering and securing clients, including Jack Maroni, 27, an MBA intern who spent four years at KKR before attending Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 来自高端金融界的人在覆盖和保护客户时会利用他们的旧关系，其中包括 27 岁的 MBA 实习生杰克·马罗尼 (Jack Maroni)，他在哈佛商学院就读之前在 KKR 工作了四年。

sentences.en: He said he's introduced Rogo to friends who are still on the buy side.
sentences.zh: 他说，他已将 Rogo 介绍给仍处于买方立场的朋友。

sentences.en: Swansen has found that his background in banking and private equity is key to keeping clients happy with Rogo, since he understands the details of their workflows.
sentences.zh: 斯旺森发现，他在银行和私募股权方面的背景是让客户对 Rogo 满意的关键，因为他了解他们的工作流程的细节。

sentences.en: Jack Maroni, 27, is getting his MBA at Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 27 岁的杰克·马罗尼 (Jack Maroni) 正在哈佛商学院攻读 MBA 学位。

sentences.en: Corrie Aune for BI
sentences.zh: BI 的 Corrie Aune

blocks.html_en: The work ethic is also similar, employees said, since many came from a world of 80-hour workweeks and, to quote Maroni, "built the muscle around grinding."

sentences.en: The work ethic is also similar, employees said, since many came from a world of 80-hour workweeks and, to quote Maroni, "built the muscle around grinding."
sentences.zh: 员工们表示，工作道德也很相似，因为许多人都来自每周工作 80 小时的世界，用马罗尼的话来说，“就是在磨砺中锻炼肌肉”。

blocks.html_en: The paycheck, however, isn't necessarily as familiar.

sentences.en: The paycheck, however, isn't necessarily as familiar.
sentences.zh: 然而，薪水不一定那么熟悉。

blocks.html_en: At Rogo, a "forward-deployed banker" in New York would earn a base salary between $115,000 and $180,000, plus potential equity and bonus, according to a job posting. Candidates are expected to have at least three years of investment banking experience at a top firm. Rogo declined to provide further details on its pay packages.

sentences.en: At Rogo, a "forward-deployed banker" in New York would earn a base salary between $115,000 and $180,000, plus potential equity and bonus, according to a job posting.
sentences.zh: 根据招聘信息，在 Rogo，纽约的“前线银行家”的基本工资为 115,000 美元至 180,000 美元，外加潜在的股权和奖金。

sentences.en: Candidates are expected to have at least three years of investment banking experience at a top firm.
sentences.zh: 候选人应在顶级公司拥有至少三年的投资银行经验。

sentences.en: Rogo declined to provide further details on its pay packages.
sentences.zh: Rogo 拒绝提供有关其薪酬方案的更多细节。

blocks.html_en: Second-year associates at top firms can make up to $400,000 all-in, Meridith Dennes, managing partner at Prospect Rock Partners, said. This year is proving especially profitable, as banks report record profits. None of the recruiters said they've seen hordes of young people leave their jobs because of anxiety about AI — banking is, Dennes said, "always going to be a stable choice."

sentences.en: Second-year associates at top firms can make up to $400,000 all-in, Meridith Dennes, managing partner at Prospect Rock Partners, said.
sentences.zh: Prospect Rock Partners 的管理合伙人 Meridith Dennes 表示，顶级公司的第二年合伙人的总收入最高可达 40 万美元。

sentences.en: This year is proving especially profitable, as banks report record profits.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，今年的利润尤其丰厚，银行公布了创纪录的利润。

sentences.en: None of the recruiters said they've seen hordes of young people leave their jobs because of anxiety about AI — banking is, Dennes said, "always going to be a stable choice."
sentences.zh: 没有一个招聘人员表示，他们看到大批年轻人因为对人工智能的焦虑而离职——丹尼斯说，银行业“永远是一个稳定的选择”。

blocks.html_en: "It is challenging to try and pull the top investment banker who's being paid an incredibly high bonus, being well taken care of. It's going to be really difficult to pull that person out unless they have a real passion for AI," said Brianne Sterling, who leads the investment banking practice at recruiting firm Selby Jennings.

sentences.en: "It is challenging to try and pull the top investment banker who's being paid an incredibly high bonus, being well taken care of.
sentences.zh: “试图拉动顶级投资银行家的工作是一项挑战，因为他的奖金高得令人难以置信，而且受到很好的照顾。

sentences.en: It's going to be really difficult to pull that person out unless they have a real passion for AI," said Brianne Sterling, who leads the investment banking practice at recruiting firm Selby Jennings.
sentences.zh: 招聘公司 Selby Jennings 投资银行业务负责人 Brianne Sterling 表示：“除非他们对人工智能有真正的热情，否则很难将其挖走。”

blocks.html_en: One key question, Keizner said, is how much equity employees get and its potential value, since cash compensation alone probably isn't enough to lure people to startups like Rogo. An equity grant in a company that succeeds could be "as lucrative, if not more lucrative, than being on a traditional finance path," he said.

sentences.en: One key question, Keizner said, is how much equity employees get and its potential value, since cash compensation alone probably isn't enough to lure people to startups like Rogo.
sentences.zh: 凯兹纳说，一个关键问题是员工获得多少股权及其潜在价值，因为仅现金补偿可能不足以吸引人们加入像 Rogo 这样的初创公司。

sentences.en: An equity grant in a company that succeeds could be "as lucrative, if not more lucrative, than being on a traditional finance path," he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，向一家成功的公司提供股权赠款可能“与走传统金融道路一样有利可图，甚至更有利可图”。

sentences.en: Aidan Donohue, a member of the engineering team, brings his dog, Billy, to the office most days.
sentences.zh: 工程团队成员艾丹·多诺霍 (Aidan Donohue) 大部分时间都会带着他的狗比利 (Billy) 来办公室。

sentences.en: Corrie Aune for BI
sentences.zh: BI 的 Corrie Aune

blocks.html_en: Navin, the head of people at Hebbia, said the compensation packages can require "a very different framing mentally" for former bankers or investors, who are more used to cash than equity. Hebbia offers bonuses for forward-deployed banking and investing roles, but they're "a lot smaller" than in traditional finance, partly because of the inclusion of equity.

sentences.en: Navin, the head of people at Hebbia, said the compensation packages can require "a very different framing mentally" for former bankers or investors, who are more used to cash than equity.
sentences.zh: 赫比亚人事主管纳文表示，对于前银行家或投资者来说，薪酬方案可能需要“一种截然不同的心理框架”，他们更习惯于现金而不是股权。

sentences.en: Hebbia offers bonuses for forward-deployed banking and investing roles, but they're "a lot smaller" than in traditional finance, partly because of the inclusion of equity.
sentences.zh: 赫比亚为前沿部署的银行和投资职位提供奖金，但这些奖金比传统金融“小得多”，部分原因是包含了股权。

blocks.html_en: More than anything, Friedman said, people struggle to give up the structure of finance. They're used to knowing what it means to do well, what the promotion path looks like, exactly how their pay will change over the years.

sentences.en: More than anything, Friedman said, people struggle to give up the structure of finance.
sentences.zh: 弗里德曼说，最重要的是，人们很难放弃金融结构。

sentences.en: They're used to knowing what it means to do well, what the promotion path looks like, exactly how their pay will change over the years.
sentences.zh: 他们习惯于知道表现出色意味着什么，晋升路径是什么样的，以及多年来他们的薪酬将如何变化。

blocks.html_en: "Convincing them that it'll be okay in a place where there's far less structure and your path might look different than your neighbor's — having that conversation with folks, some people definitely have to get over that mental barrier that unstructured things can be good," she said.

sentences.en: "Convincing them that it'll be okay in a place where there's far less structure and your path might look different than your neighbor's — having that conversation with folks, some people definitely have to get over that mental barrier that unstructured things can be good," she said.
sentences.zh: 她说：“让他们相信，在一个结构性少得多的地方，你的道路可能与邻居的道路可能有所不同，这是没问题的——通过与人们的交谈，有些人肯定必须克服这种心理障碍，即非结构化的事物可能是好的。”

年轻的银行家面临着新的选择。

华尔街传统上为初级员工提供了一条清晰但艰苦的职业道路：获得实习机会，在投资银行工作两年，然后决定是留在银行业、转到买方还是获得 MBA 学位。 人工智能现在不仅扰乱了工作的日常性质，而且还可能在金融职业道路上开辟一个新的岔路，因为一些年轻的金融家纷纷涌向金融公司的人工智能初创公司。

27 岁的贾里德·斯旺森 (Jared Swansen) 一月份跳槽到了 Rogo，这是这些初创公司之一。 此后，他忘记了作为银行家和投资者时使用的所有 Excel 快捷方式，现在他花在打字上的时间改为与他以前坐在对面的人打电话，教他们如何减少交易中的苦差事。

“圣杯是进入买方。 这是每个人的梦想，”斯旺森说。他在美国银行工作了大约三年，然后转到一家小型买方公司。 “这正是我所希望的，进行所有分析并处理不同的交易，就像我开始银行职业生涯时所希望的那样。 但很难不看到人工智能正在发生的事情。”

Rogo 于 2021 年由来自 Lazard 和摩根大通的 20 多岁前投资银行家创立，并在 4 月份的 D 轮融资后获得了 20 亿美元的估值。 该公司将领域专业知识视为一大吸引力，因为劳动力主要由工程师和斯旺森等前金融家组成。 根据员工的 LinkedIn 个人资料，他们来自 Evercore、高盛和花旗等公司。

罗戈的领导层并不期望或不希望所有银行家或私人市场投资者突然跳槽加入初创公司——这一现实会侵蚀他们的客户群。 金融行业的招聘人员并没有看到年轻员工大规模流失，不过他们表示，对于更具创业精神的人来说，人工智能正在成为越来越有吸引力的选择。 然而，离开这条规划完善、利润丰厚的金融之路也会带来风险。

“这取决于这种现象的普遍性和广泛性。 这很难量化。”招聘公司 Odyssey Search Partners 的联合创始人安东尼·凯兹纳 (Anthony Keizner) 说道。

Rogo 拥有 300 多家客户，包括 Lazard、Moelis 和 Tiger Global，并且可以自动化大部分繁琐的工作，例如制作幻灯片、进行研究和构建模型。 用户可以像对待同事一样，通过电子邮件将指令发送给人工智能代理 Felix。

垂直金融人工智能领域还有其他参与者。 Hebbia 和 Farsight AI 等竞争对手也承诺加快工作速度，而包括 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 在内的大型人工智能实验室正在聘请银行家为金融公司提供服务。

Rogo 有点像科技与金融的混搭——前银行家穿着牛仔裤四处走动，享受每日免费午餐，而工程师则在名为“戴蒙”和“索罗斯”的会议室里苦苦钻研财务时间。 当被问及他们是在金融公司还是科技公司工作时，接受本文采访的四名员工停了下来，人才主管艾尔莎·麦克莱恩 (Elsa McLean) 最终选择了“一家人工智能公司”。

30 岁的麦克莱恩表示，她不再需要对潜在的新员工进行有关 Rogo 用途的教育，并且从今年上半年开始，“入境申请数量大幅增加”。 该公司去年员工人数增加了一倍，达到 150 多人，并计划在未来 12 个月内再次增加一倍。 该公司在纽约和伦敦设有办事处，并计划在旧金山和新加坡开设办事处。

Hebbia 成立于 2020 年，拥有投资、银行和更广泛的交易生态系统（包括法律）的客户。 它还实现了快速增长：该初创公司拥有约 200 名员工，而一年前只有不到 100 名员工。 人事主管 Tom Navin 表示，今年每月入境申请数量几乎增加了两倍，达到平均 7,000 份，大约 60% 的员工拥有金融背景。

斯旺森在高中四年级时“迷上了”金融行业，并希望开创传统的职业生涯。 他第一次发现 Rogo 是在 Acacia Research 担任投资者时，虽然离开并不容易，但成为技术转型中心的想法更令人兴奋。

27 岁的雷切尔·弗里德曼 (Rachel Friedman) 作为八名员工之一、也是第一位女性来到 Rogo 时，并没有放弃她先入为主的未来。 她在杰富瑞 (Jefferies) 担任了两年多的投资银行家，她知道自己不想留在金融业，尽管她很高兴自己从那里开始。

对她来说，罗戈更多的是加入一个有趣的、快节奏的地方，在那里她可以扮演任何角色，还有一个额外的好处，就是偶尔把裤子换成运动裤。 现在从 Rogo 开始，拥有大牌投资者和全球办事处，这并不完全是一场赌博。

“我的印象是，候选人的风险状况随着时间的推移发生了相当大的变化，”弗里德曼说。 “现在，每个人都对每个金融机构都将采用人工智能的想法感到满意。 风险在于押注于正确的人。 显然，我们对此感觉非常好。”

斯旺森说，当他加入罗戈时，“感觉更大的风险可能是当整个世界都在变化时什么也不做。”

从某些方面来说，在 Rogo 工作与在顶级金融公司工作并没有什么不同，弗里德曼表示，大多数人并不认为这与金融业有任何区别。 累计工作时间相似，但员工通常对工作时间有更多的控制权。

“我工作很多，但下午 6 点我从不害怕。 周五，有什么事情会爆炸并毁掉我的周末，”斯旺森说。 “我想如果我愿意的话，我可以每天提前三个小时结束工作。 但因为我们发展得非常快，所以到处都有很棒的机会。” （斯旺森的老板弗里德曼担心他工作太多，因为他通常要工作到凌晨 1:00 左右。）

来自高端金融界的人在覆盖和保护客户时会利用他们的旧关系，其中包括 27 岁的 MBA 实习生杰克·马罗尼 (Jack Maroni)，他在哈佛商学院就读之前在 KKR 工作了四年。 他说，他已将 Rogo 介绍给仍处于买方立场的朋友。 斯旺森发现，他在银行和私募股权方面的背景是让客户对 Rogo 满意的关键，因为他了解他们的工作流程的细节。

员工们表示，工作道德也很相似，因为许多人都来自每周工作 80 小时的世界，用马罗尼的话来说，“就是在磨砺中锻炼肌肉”。

然而，薪水不一定那么熟悉。

根据招聘信息，在 Rogo，纽约的“前线银行家”的基本工资为 115,000 美元至 180,000 美元，外加潜在的股权和奖金。 候选人应在顶级公司拥有至少三年的投资银行经验。 Rogo 拒绝提供有关其薪酬方案的更多细节。

Prospect Rock Partners 的管理合伙人 Meridith Dennes 表示，顶级公司的第二年合伙人的总收入最高可达 40 万美元。 事实证明，今年的利润尤其丰厚，银行公布了创纪录的利润。 没有一个招聘人员表示，他们看到大批年轻人因为对人工智能的焦虑而离职——丹尼斯说，银行业“永远是一个稳定的选择”。

“试图拉动顶级投资银行家的工作是一项挑战，因为他的奖金高得令人难以置信，而且受到很好的照顾。 招聘公司 Selby Jennings 投资银行业务负责人 Brianne Sterling 表示：“除非他们对人工智能有真正的热情，否则很难将其挖走。”

凯兹纳说，一个关键问题是员工获得多少股权及其潜在价值，因为仅现金补偿可能不足以吸引人们加入像 Rogo 这样的初创公司。 他说，向一家成功的公司提供股权赠款可能“与走传统金融道路一样有利可图，甚至更有利可图”。

赫比亚人事主管纳文表示，对于前银行家或投资者来说，薪酬方案可能需要“一种截然不同的心理框架”，他们更习惯于现金而不是股权。 赫比亚为前沿部署的银行和投资职位提供奖金，但这些奖金比传统金融“小得多”，部分原因是包含了股权。

弗里德曼说，最重要的是，人们很难放弃金融结构。 他们习惯于知道表现出色意味着什么，晋升路径是什么样的，以及多年来他们的薪酬将如何变化。

她说：“让他们相信，在一个结构性少得多的地方，你的道路可能与邻居的道路可能有所不同，这是没问题的——通过与人们的交谈，有些人肯定必须克服这种心理障碍，即非结构化的事物可能是好的。”
